clusters.text: Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh complete major trade between PBKS and MI In a marquee player trade ahead of the TATA IPL 2027, Mumbai Indians (MI) captain Hardik Pandya will move to Punjab Kings (PBKS), while Arshdeep Singh, India’s leading wicket-taker in T20 Internationals, will join the five-time champions. Pandya’s trade brings the curtain down on his second stint with MI, a franchise with which he won four IPL titles. Having first joined MI in 2015, Pandya developed into one of the league’s most impactful all-rounders, contributing with both bat and ball during the team’s title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. After seven seasons with Mumbai, Pandya moved to Gujarat Titans (GT) ahead of IPL 2022 and made an immediate impact as captain, leading the franchise to the title in its debut season. GT also reached the final in 2023 before Pandya returned to MI in 2024 and took over the captaincy. Across 162 IPL matches, he has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and claimed 82 wickets, underlining his value as a proven match-winner. Arshdeep, meanwhile, moves to MI after eight seasons with PBKS, the franchise where he made his IPL debut in 2019 and established himself as one of the competition’s leading left-arm fast bowlers. With 111 wickets in 96 IPL matches, he is PBKS’ all-time leading wicket-taker. Arshdeep’s ability to make early breakthroughs with the new ball and deliver under pressure in the death overs has made him a key component of Punjab’s bowling attack. He claimed 21 wickets in IPL 2025 and followed that with 14 wickets in the 2026 season. His left-arm pace and ability to deliver across different phases of an innings will add considerable depth to MI’s bowling attack. Pandya will join PBKS at a fee of ₹18 crore, up from his existing fee of ₹16.35 crore, while Arshdeep will join MI at his existing fee of ₹18 crore.

clusters.title: Lawson made sure Red Bull saw he helped Verstappen in Brazil after their Mexico incident | Formula 1
clusters.snippet: Liam Lawson drew attention to one of the clearest examples of Racing Bulls helping Red Bull in the Brazilian Grand Prix.
clusters.text: 11th November 2026, 7:15 10th November 2026, 23:22 | Written by Keith Collantine “When you’re fighting for your seat, it’s not very smart behaviour,” remarked Max Verstappen after Liam Lawson refused to get out of his way during practice in Mexico last week . It’s not uncommon to see drivers make way for their team mates when ordered to on the radio. In the same race Isack Hadjar slowed significantly to let Verstappen in the other Red Bull past. Lawson, in theory at least, drives for a rival team and has no need to be helpful at all. But while a midfield team driver such as Lawson would likely see no benefit from wasting time and tyre life fighting one of the front-running cars, nor would they be expected to cost themselves time by slowing down. “Don’t lose time with him” is typical advice from race engineers. Yet that is precisely what Lawson did. Racing Bulls made sure he was aware how quickly Verstappen was gaining on him. Then Lawson dived out of the way on the Reta Oposta back straight, slowing down so much he dropped down two gears and lost over one-and-a-half seconds. Job done, he pointed out to race engineer Alexandre Iliopoulos he had not cost Verstappen any time: Lawson is still waiting to learn if he will remain at Red Bull’s junior team next year. He clearly wanted to demonstrate he is ready to help Racing Bulls’ sister team. He was much more prepared to fight his corner in Miami earlier this year, when he challenged Racing Bulls’ order that he let Verstappen past . But Lawson’s eagerness to show his worth to Red Bull also highlights how unusual their arrangement with their junior team is. One driver pulling over and slowing down so blatantly to let a driver from a rival team overtake him – and then drawing attention to it – would be astonishing if it involved any other pair of teams on the grid. clusters.snippet: Days after Carlos Alcaraz won his first Paris Masters title, the former world No. 8 said on the Nothing Major podcast that the Spaniard still has plenty of room to grow on serve. He pointed to the way Novak Djokovic improved his own delivery late in his career.
clusters.text: Days after Carlos Alcaraz won his first Paris Masters title, the former world No. 8 said on the Nothing Major podcast that the Spaniard still has plenty of room to grow on serve. He pointed to the way Novak Djokovic improved his own delivery late in his career. Carlos Alcaraz heads to the ATP Finals in Turin on the back of titles in Vienna and Paris . But for John Isner , one of the biggest servers in the history of the game, the world No. 3 still has a clear area to work on. “He can get better. His serve can still get better. I still think his serve can improve so much,” Isner said on the latest episode of the Nothing Major podcast, as reported by Tennishead . When you watch him from the back of the court, it is like, ‘How can anyone play this sport better?’” Isner pointed to Novak Djokovic as proof that a serve can be transformed during a career. “You saw Novak improve his serve in the middle towards late on in his career, and he just went boom,” the American said. Alcaraz has not waited for the advice. Ahead of the Laver Cup in September, he adjusted his service motion, with a lower ball toss and a change in the position of his left foot. Asked about it in a recent press conference, the Spaniard explained that he wanted to copy what he had seen in the greatest servers. “I have watched the best servers in history. Obviously height matters, how tall you are. But the best servers all have that balance, from the back going forward,” he said. “I wasn’t able to do that before, so I changed the motion a little bit. I tried to have more balance and to make the movement smoother. I would say the toss and the balance are everything on the serve.” “I have been feeling much better on the serve, and I think in Vienna we could see a great improvement on that shot. I’m just really happy about it.” The ATP statistics over the past 52 weeks partly back Isner up. Alcaraz ranks 13th on the tour in the ATP’s Serve Rating. He is inside the top 10 for first serves in (7th), second-serve points won (8th) and service games won (6th), but only 39th for first-serve points won and 59th for aces per match, with an average of 4.8. Those figures cover a full year, most of it before the change. In Paris, Alcaraz beat Alex Michelsen, Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud and Ben Shelton on his way to the title. The ATP Finals start on Sunday, November 15, with the group draw on Thursday.

clusters.title: Blue Line Metro Trial Operations Move Closer To Mainline Testing With Runs From Byappanahalli To KR Puram
clusters.text:
The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited has moved a step closer to mainline testing on the Blue Line, with trial runs progressing from Byappanahalli towards KR Puram and Doddanekundi, Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda confirmed.

The 58.19 km corridor is designed to connect Central Silk Board with Kempegowda International Airport via the city's technology belt.

The minister shared the update on Deepavali, stating the government is committed to completing all pending works and bringing the Blue Line into public service at the earliest.

Kinematic test runs are expected in November 2026, whilst the Blue Line's 33kV cables and third rail are being progressively charged from 30 October between Baiyappanahalli depot and Marathahalli.

The 19.75 km Phase 2A section between Central Silk Board and KR Puram is targeted to open by mid-2027, with the full corridor to the airport expected to become operational by March 2028.

BMRCL aims to run trial trains from Byappanahalli depot via KR Puram to Marathahalli by 15 November, though signalling integration remains the key hurdle before full testing can commence.

The corridor will feature 29 stations serving major employment centres whilst connecting with other Namma Metro corridors and providing a direct metro link to the airport.

Both the Blue Line's Outer Ring Road corridor and the Pink Line's underground stretch are expected to open by May 2027. Construction on the Blue Line began in August 2021 after earlier contractual setbacks.

Work on the corridor is largely complete apart from signalling, whilst around 2 km of track installation and construction work at some stations remain pending.

The elevated metro line will traverse Bengaluru's bustling Outer Ring Road technology corridor, home to numerous IT firms and residential hubs, before branching towards the airport terminal in the second phase.

clusters.text: Scott McTominay has revealed he was in hospital under sedation to have a “shock on my heart” just 48 hours before Scotland began their World Cup campaign against Haiti in June. At the time McTominay’s absence from training was put down to a stomach complaint. It emerged in August that the Napoli midfielder needed surgery to remedy an irregular heartbeat. The operation took place in September, causing McTominay to miss Scotland’s first four Nations League matches. The player has now said the matter arose in the US as Scotland prepared for their World Cup opener at Boston Stadium. McTominay is back in the international fold for Scotland’s fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland. Talking to media in Glasgow the 29-year-old said: “The World Cup was difficult for me to be honest. I had to go and get the shock on my heart. It was two days before the Haiti game and you have prepared so well. I was in such good condition and then something like that happens. And you think: ‘How is this happening to me?’ But then you have to get on with it. “These are cards you are dealt in football. Sometimes things don’t go your way and you have to continue to do your best. It’s nowhere near an excuse but it’s something you have to look back on and say it’s part of the process. “Whenever you are sitting in a hospital bed two days before the first game at the World Cup, about to get put to sleep it’s not ideal is it? When things like that happen it is what it is, there’s nothing you can do about it. After the World Cup I reflected on it and it’s probably the most disappointed I have been in my career.” Scotland were knocked out in the group stage , with McTominay’s performances among those criticised. A poor campaign also led to the resignation of Steve Clarke as manager. Sébastien Pocognoli, Clarke’s successor, will call on McTominay for the first time when North Macedonia visit Hampden Park on Friday. McTom­inay returned to the Napoli team in early October. clusters.text: Northern Ireland are top of Nations League Group B2 after four games Despite being together for 16 straight days only a month ago, when Northern Ireland players reconvened this week for Nations League fixtures against Ukraine and Hungary there was still plenty of catching up to do. Whether it be Pierce Charles' incredible double-save of Jarrod Bowen's penalty to preserve a point for Queens Park Rangers against West Ham, Isaac Price putting his own spot-kick woe behind him back at West Bromwich Albion, or Terry Devlin's double for Portsmouth against Swansea, there have been memorable moments aplenty for Michael O'Neill's squad back in club colours. Most pleasing to the manager, however, will likely be the game time currently enjoyed by his players. O'Neill has never shied away from the importance of a player's club situation to their international ambitions and, almost four years after his return to the Northern Ireland job, the message has clearly hit home. Of what is a 24-man squad for games against Ukraine on Saturday and Hungary three days later, nine players made either a permanent or loan switch during the summer. And while once the former Stoke City boss had to heavily rely on players who were getting precious few minutes in between international windows, now the group is full of regulars across England top three divisions. clusters.text: American Express has reversed course on its controversial Membership Rewards points clawback , promising affected cardmembers that it will restore the points deducted from their accounts within a week. The decision comes barely 48 hours after the company removed millions of reward points from customer accounts, citing a technical issue that had allowed points associated with previously cancelled cards to remain available beyond the permitted redemption period. The reversal is a significant climbdown for American Express, which initially maintained that the deductions complied with its Membership Rewards programme terms and conditions. The company had told affected customers that points linked to cancelled cards needed to be redeemed within 30 days of card cancellation and that any remaining points were liable to be forfeited. However, the scale of the deductions and how they were implemented triggered considerable backlash among long-standing American Express customers. According to communications shared by affected cardmembers, American Express has now committed to restoring the Membership Rewards balances to their position as of November 8, 2026. The restoration is expected to be completed within a week, effectively reversing the November 9 adjustments. The controversy began on November 9, when American Express customers started discovering substantial deductions in their Membership Rewards accounts. The company explained that a technical issue had allowed points earned on previously cancelled cards to remain visible in customers’ accounts beyond the 30-day redemption window. Once it identified the issue, Amex adjusted the balances to remove points it considered ineligible. For customers with multiple American Express cards, however, this was not straightforward. Customers could accumulate points through their Gold Card and Membership Rewards Credit Card, for instance, and redeem them from a consolidated balance. clusters.text: Students and scientists at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) Allahabad, Prayagraj, have developed a unique robotic car that can automatically expand or shrink its size according to the requirements of different situations. The innovative vehicle will be able to maneuver in areas where traditional vehicles can't get through, including narrow passages and confined spaces. A prototype of the robotic car has been created and a patent application is in process for the technology. The car has been developed by BTech students Diya Dutta and Kashish Jadhav under Dr. Surya Prakash of Information Technology (IT) branch, and is named Swerve Drive. The body structure of the robotic car can be expanded and contracted with a scissor-like mechanism, which allows the car to achieve the desired shape. If extra space is required to transport items, equipment or other materials, the vehicle can be expanded. Likewise, it can shrink in size to navigate a tight road, tight passageways and tight areas. The Swerve Drive robotic car is an adaptable design that could be used in cases where a regular car's mobility is affected. Swerve drive robotic car: Key features One of the major features of the Swerve Drive is its expandable and retractable body structure. The scissor-like opening and closing mechanism allows for the vehicle to change its size based on the environment and the need for transportation. When a larger structure is needed, the technology can be implemented to also expand the luggage and equipment carrying space of the vehicle. It can reduce in size to allow easy movement when operating in confined spaces. Special wheels allow movement in different directions Another important feature of the Swerve Drive robotic car is its specially designed wheels, which can rotate in different directions. This setup should enhance the handling characteristics of the vehicle, making it easier to handle and navigate, especially in tight spaces. The robotic vehicle, unlike conventional cars, is taking on the responsibility of turning more efficiently for its main purpose of moving forward and backward. Its wheel mechanism can also support movement across challenging surfaces, including rugged roads, hilly regions and slopes. clusters.text: The unique armour worn by Lord Ram (Ranbir Kapoor) and Lakshman (Ravi Dubey) in the grand action and war scenes of the film 'Ramayana' has become a talking point. Seen during the battle with Khara and Dushan, the armour was not made from any modern machine-made material or plastic, but was entirely handcrafted by traditional artisans using bamboo and natural fibres from the Northeast. Young designer Sagar Shreedh, a resident of Dhurwa in Ranchi, played a key role, alongside costume designer Ajay Kumar, in designing this special natural armour and bringing it to life on screen. He worked on it as the first costume assistant. Sagar, who won the Best Design Collection award while studying at NIFT Shillong, shared his experience and the complete inside story of creating the armour with City Bhaskar. Sagar says that for Ram and Lakshman's exile look, they could use only natural materials such as cane and bamboo so that flexibility could be maintained. Trials began with bamboo and "water hyacinth" based on the handicraft experience gained while studying at NIFT Shillong. Skilled artisan Jainul Abdeen prepared the first armour structure using fine bamboo weaving. To get it corrected and ensure a perfect fit, five to six trips were made from Mumbai to Guwahati and Barpeta. clusters.text: Prayagraj: Though bursting of firecrackers on Diwali did not cause an overall violation of noise limits in Prayagraj, the air quality worsened sharply within 24 hours after the festival. The average air quality index (AQI) rose from moderate on Diwali to poor the next day.The city’s average AQI was recorded at 148.67 on Diwali, Nov 8, compared with 171.33 on Nov 7, but rose sharply to 248 on Nov 9. The three monitoring stations showed a mixed trend before and during Diwali, followed by a rise at all locations on the following day.The Regional Office station recorded an AQI of 143 on Nov 7, 113 on Nov 8 and 228 on Nov 9. At Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology, the readings were 114, 114 and 222 respectively, while the Nagar Nigam station recorded 257, 219 and 294. The AQI report places 101-200 in the ‘moderate’ category and 201-300 in the ‘poor’ category.The sharpest post-Diwali rise was recorded at the Nagar Nigam monitoring station, where AQI increased from 219 on Nov 8 to 294 on Nov 9. At the Regional Office, the reading more than doubled from 113 to 228, while MNNIT recorded an increase from 114 to 222. The city average similarly increased by nearly 100 points, from 148.67 to 248.The noise monitoring exercise conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board between 6 pm and 10 pm on Diwali showed that the impact varied considerably according to the location.
